questions.title: Front and Rear of the Queue
questions.description:
A queue serves from the front and accepts at the rear — identify both endpoints.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void front_rear(const int *q, int n, int *f, int *r)

It must store q[0] (the front) into *f and q[n-1] (the rear) into *r. The harness prints both.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated values in queue order.

Output Format:
One line with the front, then the rear, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Free Slots in a Circular Queue
questions.description:
A circular queue of fixed capacity still has room until its size reaches the capacity.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int free_slots(int capacity, int size)

It must return capacity - size, the number of further enqueue operations that succeed.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: capacity and current size.

Output Format:
One line with the free slot count.

Constraints:
0 <= size <= capacity <= 100000

questions.title: Push-Front Arrival Order
questions.description:
A deque can accept elements at the front. Pushing every arriving element to the FRONT reverses the arrival order.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void push_front_order(const int *vals, int n, int *out)

It must fill out with the deque contents after pushing all n values at the front in arrival order (out[i] = vals[n-1-i]). The harness prints out.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated arrival values.

Output Format:
One line with the deque contents front to back, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Rear Insertion Index
questions.description:
In a circular queue backed by an array of capacity C, the rear insertion position wraps around using the modulo operator.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int rear_index(int capacity, int front, int size)

It must return (front + size) % capacity, the array index where the next enqueue lands.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: capacity, front index and current size.

Output Format:
One line with the insertion index.

Constraints:
1 <= capacity <= 100000, 0 <= front < capacity, 0 <= size <= capacity

questions.title: Sum of the First k Served
questions.description:
The first k elements of a queue are served in order; total up their values.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int sum_served(const int *q, int n, int k)

It must return q[0] + q[1] + ... + q[k-1].

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated queue values.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the sum of the first k values.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 1 <= k <= n, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Front After k Serves
questions.description:
After k people are served from the front, the person now at the front is the (k+1)-th arrival.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int front_after_k(const int *q, int n, int k)

It must return q[k] (0-based; k is strictly less than n).

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated queue values.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the new front value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= k < n, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Ticket Counter Next Token
questions.description:
A helpdesk issues tokens 1..issued. Each served customer consumes the smallest outstanding token.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int next_token(int issued, int served)

It must return the token that will be served next, or -1 when every issued token has been served.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: issued and served.

Output Format:
One line with the next token number or -1.

Constraints:
0 <= served <= issued <= 100000

questions.title: Print Job Queue Remaining Pages
questions.description:
An office printer keeps a FIFO queue of jobs with page counts. The first done jobs have already been served.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int total_remaining_pages(const int *jobs, int n, int done)

It must return the sum of pages of jobs still waiting: jobs[done..n-1].

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n page counts in queue order.
Line 3: done, the number of jobs already printed.

Output Format:
One line with the remaining page total.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= done <= n, 1 <= pages <= 500

questions.title: Waiting List Position
questions.description:
A clinic queue lists patient ids in arrival order. After some patients are served from the front, report where a given patient now stands.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int position_after(const int *q, int n, int target, int served)

It must find the 1-based position of target in q; if that position is <= served the patient is already gone, so return 0; otherwise return the new 1-based position (old position minus served). target is always present.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n distinct patient ids in queue order.
Line 3: target.
Line 4: served.

Output Format:
One line with the new position, or 0 if already served.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= served <= n

questions.title: Round-Robin Front After Rotations
questions.description:
A round-robin scheduler serves the front task and immediately re-enqueues it at the rear — one full rotation per serve. After r rotations, which task is at the front?

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int front_after_rotations(const int *q, int n, int r)

It must return q[r % n], the task that reaches the front after r rotations.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated task ids in queue order.
Line 3: r, the number of rotations.

Output Format:
One line with the front task id.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= r <= 1000000

questions.title: Reverse a Queue
questions.description:
An audit tool replays a queue of events in reverse order. Reversing a queue is a classic stack-plus-queue exercise.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void reverse_queue(const int *q, int n, int *out)

It must fill out with the queue contents in reverse order. The harness prints out.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated values in queue order.

Output Format:
One line with the reversed contents, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Locker Codes of Fives and Sixes
questions.description:
A locker system prints the first n valid locker codes: numbers made only of digits 5 and 6, listed in increasing order (5, 6, 55, 56, 65, 66, 555, ...). A queue generates them by appending 5 and 6 to each dequeued code.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void generate_56(int n, int *out)

It must fill out[0..n-1] with the first n such codes in increasing order. The harness prints them.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with n codes, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10

questions.title: Front-Back Card Interleave
questions.description:
A dealer shuffles a deck by alternating cards: front, back, front, back — until the deck is exhausted. With an odd count the middle card comes from the front.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void interleave(const int *q, int n, int *out)

It must fill out by alternately taking from the front pointer and the back pointer. The harness prints out.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated card values.

Output Format:
One line with the interleaved order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Fuel Circuit Start Point
questions.description:
Delivery trucks circle a route of n pumps. Pump i offers petrol[i] litres and the leg to the next pump costs dist[i] litres. Find the smallest pump index from which the truck can complete the full circuit (a valid start is guaranteed).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int tour_start(const int *petrol, const int *dist, int n)

It must return the smallest starting index that can traverse all n pumps and return to it.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n petrol values.
Line 3: n distance values.

Output Format:
One line with the start index.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 0 <= petrol[i], dist[i] <= 100

questions.title: Canteen Sandwich Line
questions.description:
Students stand in a FIFO line; a stack of sandwiches serves from the top. A student takes the top sandwich only if they prefer it (0 = round, 1 = long); otherwise they move to the back of the line. When nobody in line wants the top sandwich, everyone remaining goes hungry. Count the students who cannot eat.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int hungry_students(const int *students, const int *sandwiches, int n)

It must return how many students fail to get a sandwich. sandwiches[0] is the top of the stack.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n student preferences (0 or 1) in queue order.
Line 3: n sandwich types (0 or 1), top first.

Output Format:
One line with the hungry count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Replay Buffer: Reverse First k
questions.description:
A media player reverses only the first k entries of its replay queue (a stack pops them back in reverse) and keeps the rest in order.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void reverse_first_k(const int *q, int n, int k, int *out)

It must fill out with the first k entries reversed, followed by the remaining entries unchanged. The harness prints out.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated values.
Line 3: k (1 <= k <= n).

Output Format:
One line with the new queue, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 1 <= k <= n, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Network Latency Sliding Maximum
questions.description:
A network monitor reports the maximum latency recorded in every window of k consecutive probes (windows slide one probe at a time). A monotonic deque solves this in O(n).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void sliding_max(const int *arr, int n, int k, int *out)

It must fill out[j] (0 <= j <= n-k) with the maximum of arr[j..j+k-1]. The harness prints the n-k+1 results.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated probe latencies.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with n-k+1 maxima, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= latencies <= 1000

questions.title: First Non-Repeating Chat Character
questions.description:
A live chat ticker shows, after every incoming character, the first character seen exactly once so far (or '-' when every character so far repeats). A queue of candidates plus a frequency table solves it in one pass.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void first_unique_stream(const char *s, char *out)

It must fill out[i] with the first non-repeating character among s[0..i] (or '-' when none), and NUL-terminate out.

Input Format:
One token of lowercase letters.

Output Format:
One line with the per-position answers (a '-' is printed when there is no unique character).

Constraints:
1 <= length of s <= 1000, s contains only 'a'-'z'
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of s <= 1000, s contains only 'a'-'z'

questions.title: Longest Calm Window
questions.description:
A server-health tool finds the longest contiguous window of load readings whose difference between the maximum and minimum stays within a calm limit. Two monotonic deques track the window max and min.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int longest_calm(const int *arr, int n, int limit)

It must return the length of the longest window arr[l..r] with max - min <= limit.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated readings.
Line 3: limit.

Output Format:
One line with the longest calm window length.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= limit <= 1000000, -1000 <= readings <= 1000

questions.title: Smart Bulb Group Switching
questions.description:
A smart home can switch a group of k consecutive bulbs at once. Every bulb that is OFF must be turned ON with as few group switches as possible (a switch flips k consecutive bulbs). Report the minimum number of switches, or -1 if it cannot be done.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_bit_flips(const int *arr, int n, int k)

It must return the minimum number of group switches so every bulb ends ON (1 = ON, 0 = OFF), or -1 when impossible. Simulate with a queue that tracks which past switches still affect the current bulb.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n bulb states (0 or 1).
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of switches or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 2000, arr[i] is 0 or 1
